key_insight: The paper shows that online RL fine-tuning of vision-language-action (VLA) policies can be improved by turning sparse episode-level success/failure signals into hierarchical advantage weights, giving more precise learning guidance than a single scalar reward. This helps the policy keep improving even after basic task success becomes common.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of training VLAs with only binary rollout outcomes, where standard methods compress all feedback into one scalar reward/advantage and lose important transition-level distinctions needed for effective actor updates.
method: Collect online rollouts from pretrained VLA policies with only episode-level binary outcomes (success/failure).
Convert sparse outcome signals into hierarchical advantage weights that provide per-transition supervision instead of a single flat scalar.
Use the weighted advantages to guide actor updates, preserving richer feedback about which transitions helped or hurt performance.
impact: For practitioners, this offers a more informative and stable way to fine-tune VLAs when dense rewards are unavailable. It is especially useful in robotics and embodied AI settings where success labels are common but step-by-step supervision is expensive or impossible.

paper_title: Hierarchical Advantage Weighting for Online RL Fine-Tuning of VLAs from Sparse Episode Outcomes
paper_authors: Tongyan Fang, Siyuan Huang, Naiyu Fang, Ganlong Zhao, Zhongjin Luo
